## A reusable workflow for each monitoring context

Common data formats do not guarantee comparable ecological results. Decisions
about modules, parameter sharing, filters, and reporting can also differ among
sites or monitoring rounds. A profile provides a reusable, ordered reporting
workflow; its referenced modules and object settings carry the analytical
methods and parameters. Review and version all three together.

| Profile | Example context | REM parameter sharing |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | Standard ecological report | Pooled across years within species |
| `EOW` | Customised European Observatory of Wildlife workflow | Fitted separately for each species and year |

Neither profile establishes that a dataset satisfies every method's assumptions.
The EOW example is not a claim of formal network endorsement. Pooled and annual
parameters can yield different estimates; choose the approach appropriate to
your survey and document it rather than expecting profiles to be interchangeable.

## What a profile stores

A profile is a named, ordered selection of modules for `report()` and
`status()`. It lets you reuse a reporting template without moving or copying
the module files. It stores module names, their source pools, and optional
parent overrides. It does not store input data, analytical results, package
versions, or copies of the modules' code.

There are two module pools in a `camReport` object:

| Pool | Object field | Bundled source folder | Usual output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `report` | `cm$reportObjectElements$Modules` | `reportSections` | Ecological report |
| `status` | `cm$reportObjectElements$Status_modules` | `statusSections` | Data Status Check |

`report::introduction` means the module named `introduction` in the ecological
pool. `status::spatial` means the module named `spatial` in the data-status
pool. These are module references, not R namespace calls. Unqualified names
in a profile's `report` selection default to the `report` pool; those in its
`status` selection default to the `status` pool.

The attached report trees (`cm$reportObjects` and `cm$statusReportObjects`)
are the current selections used for rendering. Applying a profile rebuilds
the corresponding tree from the pools. This is why edits made only to an
attached section should be made after selecting a profile and rendered
without applying the profile again.

## Inspect bundled profiles

Use the `cm` created in the [README quick start](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/).
The following examples use temporary paths so they do not overwrite files in
your project.

```{r inspect-profiles, eval=FALSE}
library(camtrapReport)

profile_names(cm)
section_names(object = cm, profile = "default")
section_names(object = cm, profile = "EOW", report_type = "status")
section_names(object = cm, report_type = "all")
```

The `default` profile selects the standard modules, including pooled
multi-year REM parameters. `EOW` selects its customised modules, annual REM
parameters, and selected status modules in the ecological appendix. Neither
profile guarantees that the input data meet every selected method's
requirements. Review the module definitions and optional dependencies first.

`sections(cm, profile = "EOW")` lists that profile's selection. Supplying
`n` edits it; passing `profile` to `report()` or `status()` applies it while
rendering.

## Define and render a small profile

This small profile uses only bundled modules. Its ecological report contains
an introduction and methods heading, and its status report contains spatial,
temporal, and data-availability checks.

```{r create-brief-profile, eval=FALSE}
brief <- reportProfile(
  name = "brief",
  description = "A small report for a first inspection",
  report = c("introduction", "methods"),
  status = c("spatial", "temporal", "availability")
)
add_profile(cm, brief)

report(
  cm,
  profile = "brief",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "brief-report.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
status(
  cm,
  profile = "brief",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "brief-status.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
```

Keep a parent before its children. For example, `study_area` requires
`methods`, and `captures` requires `results`. Profile application reports a
missing or incorrectly ordered parent rather than silently creating one.
Inspect the hierarchy with `list_Modules()`.

## Edit a profile's selection

Supply the complete desired order through `n`. This updates the profile in
the current object; it does not change the bundled YAML definition.

```{r edit-brief-profile, eval=FALSE}
sections(
  cm,
  n = c("introduction", "methods", "study_area"),
  profile = "brief"
)
sections(cm, profile = "brief")

# The status selection is edited independently:
sections(
  cm,
  n = c("spatial", "availability"),
  profile = "brief",
  report_type = "status"
)
```

## Include status modules in an ecological report

A profile can select from either pool for either output. A `parent` override
places the status sections below a report appendix without changing their
shared YAML files. Here `appendix_eow` provides a non-tabbed appendix that
supports both HTML and PDF output.

```{r combined-profile, eval=FALSE}
entries <- data.frame(
  source = c("report", "report", "status", "status"),
  module = c("introduction", "appendix_eow", "spatial", "temporal"),
  parent = c(NA, NA, "appendix_eow", "appendix_eow"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
combined <- reportProfile(name = "combined", report = entries)
add_profile(cm, combined)
report(
  cm,
  profile = "combined",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "combined-report.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
```

Module names must be unique within each pool, and a rendered selection cannot
contain two modules with the same name across pools. Supplying a module in
`report = ...` does not change which pool it came from; the `source` field
or qualified reference resolves that explicitly.

## Share a profile

Write the profile registered in the object after editing, rather than an
older R variable that might still contain the original selection.

```{r share-brief-profile, eval=FALSE}
profile_file <- tempfile("brief-profile-", fileext = ".yml")
write_profile("brief", profile_file, object = cm)

imported <- read_profile(profile_file)
imported
# For an object with no profile named "brief":
# add_profile(other_cm, imported)
# To deliberately replace the existing profile in cm:
add_profile(cm, imported, overwrite = TRUE)
```

The YAML can be versioned and shared alongside the relevant module files.
Reading or registering a profile does not run or install its modules. Every
referenced module must already be in the receiving object's source pool.
A project folder containing custom YAML is not automatically imported by
`read_profile()` or `camData()`. For custom modules, follow the explicit
registration and attachment workflow in the
[module guide](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/modules.html).
In particular, `cm$addReportObject()` attaches a section to the current report
tree; it does not register it in a profile's source pool.

Inspect all shared modules before executing them. Their R code and embedded
text expressions run with your R session's permissions. Retain the profile,
module versions, source data, settings, and package versions to reproduce an
analysis.

## HTML and PDF compatibility

HTML remains interactive. PDF prints the HTML report using optional
`pagedown` and a supported Chrome or Edge browser. It omits the table of
contents and expands printable tab panels in sequence. Use an explicit path:

```{r profile-pdf, eval=FALSE}
report(
  cm,
  profile = "brief",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "brief-report-pdf.pdf"),
  view = FALSE
)
```

The registry's `formats` column (`html`, `pdf`, or `both`) controls which
selected modules can render. An incompatible module and children without an
available parent are excluded for that output. Check the messages and the
finished report; an HTML-only module is not automatically converted into a
new PDF-compatible analysis. `list_Modules(tree = FALSE)` shows these flags.

## Towards shared analytical practice

Projects can already share profiles alongside their required module files,
settings, data provenance, and software versions. A curated community knowledge
hub of reviewed workflows is a future direction, not an implemented service or
guarantee of methodological consensus. To propose a reusable workflow, open an
[issue](https://github.com/spatialecology/camtrapReport/issues) describing the
monitoring context, assumptions, analytical choices, and required inputs.
